postings.title: Software Engineer
postings.description:
ABOUT FLOW

Flow Engineering is an AI-native requirements platform for modern engineering organizations, enabling hardware teams to collaborate with AI agents to design, validate, and evolve complex systems with speed and rigor.


ABOUT THE ROLE

Flow is seeking software engineers to build AI-powered capabilities that help teams author, review, and manage requirements more effectively. You will work on agentic systems engineer and agentic domain engineer workflows—bringing AI into the center of how teams reason about their systems.

This role sits at the intersection of AI, product, and full-stack engineering: you will take ideas from prototype all the way to stable, observable features in production.


WHAT YOU’LL DO

 - Design and ship AI-powered features such as assisted requirement drafting, consistency checks, impact analysis, and intelligent suggestions for systems and domain engineers.

 - Build agentic workflows that help “agentic systems engineers” and “agentic domain engineers” explore designs, simulate changes, and validate requirements.

 - Evaluate and integrate language models and related tooling, optimizing for reliability, latency, cost, and debuggability in production.

 - Build and maintain the surrounding infrastructure: data pipelines, evaluation harnesses, prompt and model management, observability, and safety/guardrails.

 - Work across the stack—from backend integrations and APIs to simple UI hooks—to deliver complete AI features, not just model endpoints.

 - Partner with product and customers to identify high-value workflows, run experiments, and iterate quickly based on usage.


ABOUT YOU

 - 3+ years developing production software, including designing, testing, and operating services at scale in a cloud environment.

 - Hands-on experience with modern LLM providers and tooling (e.g., OpenAI, Anthropic, Hugging Face, vector stores, RAG patterns).

 - Familiarity with prompt design, retrieval-augmented systems, evaluation methods, and safety/guardrail approaches.

 - Ability to reason about tradeoffs between different models, architectures, and deployment patterns and make pragmatic decisions.

 - Comfortable working in a high-ownership, fast-paced environment where experiments and iteration are the norm.


OUR STACK (AI-LEANING)

 - TypeScript/Node.js and Python for AI and backend services.

 - Modern LLM APIs and orchestration libraries for building agentic workflows.

 - Postgres and other managed cloud services for data and state.


HOW WE WORK & VALUES

 - Speed over everything: prototype AI workflows quickly, then harden what works.

 - Own, downscope, ship, iterate: one clear owner per feature, from prototype to production.

 - Fundamentals done well: evaluation, observability, and safety are part of the first version, not an afterthought.

 - Competitive salary and meaningful equity.

 - Health, dental, and vision coverage.

 - Flexible time off and support for experimentation, learning, and staying current with the AI ecosystem.

postings.title: Forward Deployed Engineer
postings.description:
ABOUT FLOW

Flow is reinventing how humanity builds its most complex machines. We are the tool for complex systems engineering used by next gen teams building the future of space, defense, automotive, aviation and robotics. If a company is aiming for the Moon, developing fusion power, or establishing the first interplanetary colony, they’re likely using Flow to get there.

We’re backed by Sequoia Capital with angel investors including Patrick & John Collison (Stripe), David Helgason (Unity) and Kyle Parrish (Figma).




ABOUT THE ROLE

As one of our first forward deployed engineers, you’ll sit at the intersection of sales, engineering and customers: understanding how next-gen hardware teams build, guiding deployments, and supporting adoption, ensuring customers have the insight and tools to achieve meaningful outcomes.

This is an ideal role for someone who started their career on hardware engineering programs, then discovered they love working with customers to solve their problems. This role will enable incredible hardware companies to reinvent how they work.




WHAT YOU’LL DO

 - Owning the technical win: You will own a valuable part of the sales process (custom demos, trail/POC execution). This is paramount to winning new business for Flow. 

 - Understand and map customer workflows: Work with customers to deeply understand their current workflow, pain points, and priorities, and showcase tailored solutions to proactively address those.

 - Run technical enablement sessions: Identify and demonstrate how Flow can transform the customer’s development process through workshops, training, and joint solutions sessions.

 - Shape our roadmap: Act as the link between our customers and engineering to develop new innovative solutions. You will be key in building the future roadmap of our product by acting as the technical team’s eyes and ears in the field.

 - Build the GTM foundation: Help build and define Flow’s activation methodology for our most strategic customers. You will help design our technical GTM playbook, implementation guides, and training materials for future hires.




ABOUT YOU

 - Strong software engineering fundamentals: Including designing, testing, and operating services at scale in a cloud environment.

 - Structured storyteller: You can turn complex ideas into simple messages and make them engaging to both engineers and executives.

 - Builder mentality: You want to help define how a world-class technical GTM motion is built from the ground up.
   
   


NICE TO HAVE

 - You get systems engineering: 3+ years in a hardware, mechanical or systems engineering role. You know how complex machines are actually developed.

 - Sales experience: managed customer relationships in either pre-sales or post-sales engagements. Closing experience is an extra bonus!

 - Industry experience: Experience in industries such as space, energy, robotics, or advanced manufacturing.

 - Experience working with engineering tools like Jira, Confluence, PLM, MBSE or legacy requirements tools.

postings.title: Staff Software Engineer, Infrastructure
postings.description:
ABOUT FLOW

Flow Engineering is an AI-native requirements platform for modern engineering organizations, enabling hardware teams to collaborate with AI agents to design, validate, and evolve complex systems with speed and rigor. After a recent Series A, the team is scaling the product from thousands of users to hundreds of thousands while holding a high bar on reliability and speed.


ABOUT THE ROLE

Flow is hiring a staff software engineer with an infrastructure focus to build and scale the core platform behind Flow. You will own services and infrastructure that let “agentic systems engineers” and product teams rely on Flow in their day-to-day work.

You will join a small, senior, high-ownership team that values speed, ownership, and strong fundamentals: ship v1s quickly, learn, and iterate.


WHAT YOU’LL DO

 - Design, build, and operate backend services and platform primitives that support complex engineering workflows and collaboration at scale.

 - Scale Flow from thousands of users to hundreds of thousands, improving performance, reliability, observability, and security across the stack.

 - Own and evolve CI/CD pipelines, test infrastructure, and internal tooling so the team can ship quickly and safely.

 - Collaborate with frontend and AI engineers to define APIs, data models, and integration points that are robust and easy to evolve.

 - Contribute to architectural decisions and technical direction as the product and customer base grow.


ABOUT YOU

 - 3+ years of software engineering experience building and operating production systems in a cloud environment (e.g., AWS or GCP).

 - Strong understanding of systems design, distributed systems, reliability, observability, and security best practices.

 - Experience with containerization and infrastructure-as-code tooling (e.g., Docker, Terraform, or similar).

 - Comfortable owning projects end-to-end in a fast-paced environment and making pragmatic tradeoffs under ambiguity.

 - Collaborative, low-ego, and excited to work closely with product, design, and customer-facing teams.


OUR STACK (INFRA-LEANING)

 - TypeScript, Node.js, and React on the application side (with a strong bias toward type safety).

 - Postgres and other managed cloud services for persistence and messaging.

 - Containers, Terraform (or similar), and a major cloud provider (AWS/GCP) for infrastructure.


HOW WE WORK & VALUES

 - Speed over everything: ship v1s quickly, learn, and iterate rather than chasing perfection.

 - Own, downscope, ship, iterate: clear ownership, smallest real thing, tight feedback loops.

 - Fundamentals done well: simple, repeatable systems that let us move fast without breaking trust.

 - Competitive salary and meaningful equity.

 - Health, dental, and vision coverage.

 - Flexible time off and support for travel to customers when it matters (“get on a plane”).

ABOUT THE ROLE

Flow is seeking a strategic Account Executive to lead enterprise go-to-market efforts and win our largest, most complex accounts. You will own the full sales cycle, from prospecting and discovery through close, selling into major engineering-led organizations that build complex hardware and software systems. COMPENSATION & BENEFITS

postings.title: Solutions Architect
postings.description:
About Flow

Flow Engineering is an AI-native requirements platform for modern engineering organizations, enabling hardware teams to collaborate with AI agents to design, validate, and evolve complex systems with speed and rigor.

About the role

Flow is seeking a Solutions Architect (Sales Engineer) to be the technical partner in our sales process. Our buyers are systems and engineering leaders at aerospace, defense, automotive, and hardware companies, and they need to see how Flow fits their real workflows before they commit. You will run technical discovery, demos, and pilots, and you will be the person who can answer the hard questions in the room.

This role pairs closely with our account executives. They own the commercial relationship, and you own the technical win: showing the product, mapping it to the customer's engineering process, and making sure a pilot proves out what it needs to.

What you'll do

 - Partner with account executives on discovery calls, technical demos, and pilots, from first technical conversation through to a signed deal.

 - Understand each customer's engineering workflow and requirements process, then show how Flow fits it.

 - Build and run demos and proofs of concept that reflect the customer's actual use case rather than a generic script.

 - Answer technical and security questions from engineering, IT, and security teams, and complete security questionnaires with support from the team.

 - Work with product and engineering to feed back what customers need and where the product should go next.

 - Partner with forward deployed engineers to hand off pilots cleanly into deployment.

About you

 - 4+ years in sales engineering, solutions engineering, forward deployed engineering, or a technical customer-facing role.

 - Comfortable running a technical room, from individual engineers up to VPs, and adjusting the conversation to each.

 - Strong technical foundation: you can reason about APIs, integrations, and how software fits into an existing engineering stack.

 - Able to translate between what a customer says they need and what the product actually does.

 - Comfortable in a fast-moving environment where the sales motion and the product are both still taking shape.

Nice to have

 - Familiarity with requirements, systems engineering, PLM, or ALM tooling (Jama, DOORS, etc.)

 - Background in or selling into defense, aerospace, or regulated hardware environments.

postings.title: Senior Software Engineer - Integrations
postings.description:
About Flow

Flow Engineering is an AI-native requirements platform for modern engineering organizations, enabling hardware teams to collaborate with AI agents to design, validate, and evolve complex systems with speed and rigor.

About the role

Flow is seeking a Senior Software Engineer - Integrations to build the connections between Flow and the tools our customers already run. Our customers are hardware teams in aerospace, defense, automotive, and adjacent industries, and their engineering work lives across PLM, ALM, requirements, and issue-tracking systems. Getting Flow to work cleanly with that existing stack is often what turns a pilot into a full deployment.

This role sits between engineering, product, and our customers. You will design and ship integrations, own their reliability once they are live, and work directly with customer engineering teams to understand how their data actually moves.

What you'll do

 - Design, build, and maintain integrations connecting Flow to customer systems such as PLM and ALM platforms (Solidworks, AutoCAD), requirements tools (Jama, DOORS), issue trackers (Jira, Linear), and version control (GitHub, GitLab).

 - Build reliable data sync, including mapping, transformation, conflict handling, and keeping records consistent across systems.

 - Work directly with customer engineering and IT teams to scope integrations, understand their data models, and get deployments live.

 - Design and maintain the APIs and webhooks that let customers and partners build against Flow.

 - Own integrations in production, covering monitoring, error handling, and debugging sync issues across systems you do not control.

 - Partner with forward deployed engineers and product engineers to turn recurring customer needs into reusable integration patterns.

About you

 - 5+ years developing production software, including designing and operating services at scale in a cloud environment.

 - Experience building and maintaining integrations against third-party APIs, ideally in a customer-facing or B2B setting.

 - Strong grasp of API design (REST, webhooks, and related patterns) and the realities of syncing data between systems.

 - Comfortable debugging problems that span multiple systems, including ones where you have limited visibility.

 - Able to work directly with customers and translate their technical setup into a clear integration plan.

 - Comfortable in a high-ownership environment where you scope, build, and support your own work.

Nice to have

 - Familiarity with PLM, ALM, or systems engineering tooling

 - Exposure to defense, aerospace, or regulated hardware environments.

Our stack

 - TypeScript/Node.js and Python for backend and integration services.

 - REST and webhook-based APIs, message queues, and standard cloud infrastructure.

postings.description:
ABOUT FLOW

Flow is the systems engineering platform for the world's best hardware teams. Companies like Rivian run their programs on Flow, keeping requirements, interfaces, tests, and design decisions connected in one live system instead of scattered across documents and legacy tools. We're growing fast, backed by Sequoia, and selling into an industry that is actively rethinking how engineering work gets done.


THE ROLE

Our technical win is consultative. In mid-market and enterprise deals, our SEs run a structured two-week evaluation where they don't just prove the product works. They sit with systems engineers and chief engineers and help them redesign how their organization does engineering to move faster. When we win, it's because we’ve demonstrated to the customer a new way of working, not because we checked more feature boxes.

Right now we have a small SE team and no playbook. Deals get won, but they're won on individual effort rather than a system.

Your job is to build that machine while running deals inside it. You'll carry evaluations yourself from day one, codify what already works on the team into a playbook anyone strong can run, and then hire and ramp the team that runs it. We plan to grow from to 10+ across regions in the next 12 months. The hiring bar, the ramp program, and the eval framework are yours to design and own.

You'll report to the Head of Sales and work as a peer to our AE team. You'll also help design the handoff from technical win to deployment as we build out post-sales.


WHAT YOU'LL OWN IN YEAR ONE

 - Personally run technical evaluations on our most important deals

 - Codify the SE playbook: trial plans, workshop formats, demo environments, competitive positioning against legacy requirements tools

 - Define the SE hiring profile and hire SEs

 - Build onboarding and certification so a new SE is running evals independently within their first quarter

 - Design the technical-win-to-deployment handoff with the Head of Sales


WHO DOES WELL HERE

 - You've led a solutions engineering or solutions architecture team of roughly 4 to 10 people, and you were still in deals while you led it. If you haven't personally run an enterprise evaluation in the last year, this probably isn't the right fit.

 - You built the systems, you didn't inherit them. You can show us an onboarding program, eval framework, or demo environment you created from nothing, ideally at a company generating eight figures of ARR

 - You've hired SEs against a bar you defined, and you can talk honestly about the ones you got wrong.

 - You're credible with engineers. You've sold technical products into hardware, manufacturing, CAD/PLM/simulation, or embedded software, or you have an engineering background yourself. You don't need to be a former systems engineer, but you need to be able to hire and evaluate them.

 - You want to build at this stage. If your ideal next step is running a 50-person org you didn't build, this role will frustrate you.

postings.title: Forward Deployed Engineer
postings.description:
ABOUT FLOW

Flow is reinventing how humanity builds its most complex machines. We are the tool for complex systems engineering used by next gen teams building the future of space, defense, automotive, aviation and robotics. If a company is aiming for the Moon, developing fusion power, or establishing the first interplanetary colony, they’re likely using Flow to get there.

We’re backed by Sequoia Capital with angel investors including Patrick & John Collison (Stripe), David Helgason (Unity) and Kyle Parrish (Figma).

 


ABOUT THE ROLE

As one of our first forward deployed engineers, you’ll sit at the intersection of sales, engineering and customers: understanding how next-gen hardware teams build, guiding deployments, and supporting adoption, ensuring customers have the insight and tools to achieve meaningful outcomes.

This is an ideal role for someone who started their career on hardware engineering programs, then discovered they love working with customers to solve their problems. This role will enable incredible hardware companies to reinvent how they work.

 


WHAT YOU’LL DO

 - Owning the technical win: You will own a valuable part of the sales process (custom demos, trail/POC execution). This is paramount to winning new business for Flow. 

 - Understand and map customer workflows: Work with customers to deeply understand their current workflow, pain points, and priorities, and showcase tailored solutions to proactively address those.

 - Run technical enablement sessions: Identify and demonstrate how Flow can transform the customer’s development process through workshops, training, and joint solutions sessions.

 - Shape our roadmap: Act as the link between our customers and engineering to develop new innovative solutions. You will be key in building the future roadmap of our product by acting as the technical team’s eyes and ears in the field.

 - Build the GTM foundation: Help build and define Flow’s activation methodology for our most strategic customers. You will help design our technical GTM playbook, implementation guides, and training materials for future hires.

 


ABOUT YOU

 - Strong software engineering fundamentals: Including designing, testing, and operating services at scale in a cloud environment.

 - Structured storyteller: You can turn complex ideas into simple messages and make them engaging to both engineers and executives.

 - Builder mentality: You want to help define how a world-class technical GTM motion is built from the ground up.
   
    


NICE TO HAVE

 - You get systems engineering: 3+ years in a hardware, mechanical or systems engineering role. You know how complex machines are actually developed.

 - Sales experience: managed customer relationships in either pre-sales or post-sales engagements. Closing experience is an extra bonus!

 - Industry experience: Experience in industries such as space, energy, robotics, or advanced manufacturing.

 - Experience working with engineering tools like Jira, Confluence, PLM, MBSE or legacy requirements tools.

postings.title: Filmmaker in Residence
postings.description:
Flow is what the frontier of hardware is built on. We're building a new way to engineer machines — alongside the teams inventing what the world hasn't seen in aerospace, robotics, energy, and the categories that haven't been named yet. We're hiring a filmmaker to tell this story.

What you'll own

You'll shape how Flow shows up to the world. Day to day, that means:

 - Narrative direction. You hold the through-line. The podcast, the customer films, the social cuts should feel like chapters of one bigger story

 - Podcast production. Record, edit, and publish conversations between our founder and the engineering leaders building the most ambitious hardware in the world. You own the production (including cutting the clips that travel)

 - Customer films. Not case studies. Short, cinematic pieces that let the viewer feel what it's like inside the companies we serve. More A24 than B2B.

 - Social-first video. Short-form content that doesn't look like a startup made it. Our feed should read like a visual essay, not a demo reel.

Who we're looking for

 - A creative first. You see things other people miss, and you make them visible.

 - A storyteller. You know what makes a moment matter, and how to shape a thread the viewer can't look away from. A great eye. You can't always articulate why a shot works, but you know.

 - A great eye. You can't always articulate why a shot works, but you know.

 - A few years of production experience (but what you've shipped matters more than how long you’ve worked)

 - Comfort owning the whole stack: shoot, edit, color, sound, delivery. No crew to hide behind.

 - Hardware interest is a plus, not a prerequisite. We can teach you about rockets. We can't teach taste.

What this isn't

 - A role for someone who wants to be told what to shoot.

Send a reel or three pieces you're proud of, plus one paragraph on why they matter to you.
No cover letter. No CV required.

postings.title: Sales Director
postings.description:
ABOUT FLOW

Flow Engineering is an AI-native requirements platform for modern engineering organizations, enabling hardware teams to collaborate with AI agents to design, validate, and evolve complex systems with speed and rigor.


ABOUT THE ROLE

Flow is hiring a Director of Sales to build and lead our sales team as we scale go-to-market. You will be a player-coach: closing our largest, most complex deals yourself while hiring, mentoring, and developing the Account Executives who will carry Flow into major engineering-led organizations that build complex hardware and software systems. This role is an opportunity to define how Flow sells, set the standard for the team, and directly shape our commercial trajectory at an early stage.


WHAT YOU'LL DO

 - Build the sales team: recruit, hire, and onboard Account Executives, and tap your network to attract top talent.

 - Mentor and develop your reps through deal coaching, call reviews, and hands-on support in complex deals.

 - Stay close to the deals: personally lead and close strategic opportunities alongside the team.

 - Own the number: set targets, build the forecast, manage the pipeline, and hold the team accountable to plan.

 - Run complex, multi-threaded deals across technical, executive, and procurement stakeholders, often spanning long cycles and multi-year contracts.

 - Build land-and-expand motions across named enterprise accounts in engineering, hardware, and aerospace/defense.

 - Partner with engineering to relay customer feedback and influence the roadmap.

 - Collaborate with leadership on positioning, pricing, territory design, and go-to-market strategy.

 - Represent Flow at industry events, conferences, and customer meetings.

 - 30–50% travel expected.


ABOUT YOU

 - 3+ years managing and developing a team of quota-carrying sellers, ideally as a Head of Sales at an early-stage company or a Director of Sales at a Series B (or similar) company.

 - 8+ years of B2B SaaS sales experience, including a strong personal track record closing large, complex enterprise deals.

 - You've hired, coached, and retained high-performing AEs, and people you've managed would want to work with you again.

 - Consistent record of you and your team hitting or exceeding quota.

 - Comfortable with six- and seven-figure deals and with formal procurement, security, and legal review.

 - Experience selling to technical or engineering buyers.

 - Strong discovery and consultative selling skills: you listen first, lead with customer problems, and teach others to do the same.

 - A strong professional network you can draw on to build the team.

 - Comfortable in a high-ownership, fast-paced environment where you build process as you go.

 - Familiarity with engineering, PLM, or requirements management tools is a plus.


HOW WE WORK & VALUES

 - Speed over everything: move fast, run experiments, learn quickly.

 - Own, downscope, ship, iterate: one clear owner per deal and initiative, from first contact to close.

 - Fundamentals done well: rigorous discovery, clear documentation, and thoughtful follow-through are part of every deal, not an afterthought.


COMPENSATION & BENEFITS

 - Competitive salary and meaningful equity.

 - Health, dental, and vision coverage.

 - Flexible time off and support for continued learning and staying current with the AI ecosystem.
